_meta.description: Config SSOT for the enviroplus backup lane. Two sources with different shapes: enviro.db is a single live SQLite file needing a consistent snapshot, raw-capture is an append-only tree whose current day is still being written. They replicate by different verbs for that reason, not by preference. The tree's files are NOT immutable -- today's partition grows all day, and treating it as immutable is what broke this lane in production.
principles: Verification is by remote hash, never by exit code. rclone exiting 0 is not evidence the bytes arrived.
No enumerated backup target list: sources are declared here as a set, and a new source is a new entry rather than an edit to code.
Timeouts are off-nominal guards sized so a nominal run never reaches them.
A run that cannot prove what landed fails loud and leaves no manifest.
changelog: 2026-08-06 20:33  Claude  [Fix] Delete staged snapshots on verified upload. retention_count=7 guarded a working set with no readers.

2026-08-07 06:55  Claude  [Fix] Config described the tree lane as syncing immutable files; it copies, and today's partition is appended to all day. Success path now clears the whole staging pattern, and dry-run branches before the snapshot is created.

database.comment: VACUUM INTO, never a file copy. The database is journal_mode=WAL with four concurrent writers; a naive copy is torn and its hash would certify the torn artifact.

raw_capture.comment: Canonical tier, append-only. Replicated by copy, never sync: sync deletes remote objects absent locally, so a truncated source would destroy the offsite copy and the following check would pass because both sides now agree. Each file is verified by prefix AND progress -- the remote must be a prefix of the local file and no shorter than that file was when the run began. A tarball would re-upload the whole corpus every run.

local_staging.comment: Snapshots are staged locally so the uploaded artifact is the one whose hash was computed. A verified upload clears every staged snapshot for that source, not just the current run's: a snapshot kept to explain a failure has no purpose once a later run succeeds, and removing only the current file left those to accumulate for good. A failed run keeps its snapshot for diagnosis, bounded by failed_run_retention so a persistently failing remote cannot fill the disk.
